title: The Twelve Olympians
objective: After this level you can name the main Greek gods and what each ruled.
summary: The Greeks said their twelve great gods lived on Mount Olympus, Greece’s highest peak; the lists of the twelve varied, and the gods looked and acted like people.

cards.headline: The Greek gods had a real address: the highest mountain in Greece.
cards.body: Who was said to live up there, what did each one rule, and who got a seat at the table?

cards.headline: A home on the highest peak
cards.body: Remember Level 2? Mountains cover about four-fifths of Greece. The Greeks gave their gods the tallest one. Mount Olympus rises 2,917 m (9,570 feet), the highest peak in Greece, and they regarded it as the home of the gods and the site of Zeus’s throne. That’s why the great gods are called the Olympians. In a land full of mountains, the gods took the penthouse.

mascot.line: Best view in Greece, and nobody upstairs to complain about the noise!

items.label: Big realms
points: Zeus: the sky and the weather, with his thunderbolt
Hera: queen of the gods and goddess of marriage

items.label: Craftsman and courier
points: Hephaestus: fire, and the forge where he made the gods’ weapons
Hermes: messenger of the gods, protector of travelers and trade

cards.headline: The twelfth seat
cards.body: Ask the Greeks to name all twelve and you’d get more than one answer. One common list runs Zeus, Hera, Poseidon, Demeter, Athena, Apollo, Artemis, Ares, Aphrodite, Hephaestus, Hermes and Dionysus. Other lists seat Hestia, goddess of the hearth, or even Hades instead. Twelve chairs, and the guest list kept changing.

cards.headline: Gods who acted like people
cards.body: What made these gods feel so Greek? Greek religion pictured many gods in human form, with one supreme god over them. They looked like people, and they behaved like people too. In Greek stories Hera, queen of the gods, keeps appearing as Zeus’s jealous, vengeful wife, hounding the women he loved. Gods, yes, but with very human tempers.

cards.headline: The Olympians: seated
learned: The gods lived on Mount Olympus, Greece’s highest peak
Zeus sky, Poseidon sea, Hera marriage, Demeter grain
The gods looked and acted like people

questions.prompt: Where did the Greeks say their great gods lived?

options.label: Deep under the Aegean Sea
options.rationale: The sea was Poseidon’s realm, not the gods’ home.

options.label: In a palace in the clouds over Athens
On Mount Olympus, Greece’s highest peak
On an island at the edge of the world
options.rationale: Olympus is on the Greek mainland.

questions.explanation: The Greeks regarded Mount Olympus, the highest mountain in Greece, as the home of the gods and the site of Zeus’s throne.

questions.prompt: Why is there no single answer to the question “Who were the twelve Olympians?”

options.label: Greek lists of the twelve didn’t always agree
The Greeks never named any of their gods
options.rationale: They named plenty; the lists differed.

options.label: The Romans picked the twelve centuries later
Only Zeus was thought to live on Olympus
options.rationale: All twelve were said to live there.

questions.explanation: One common list includes Dionysus, while others seat Hestia, goddess of the hearth, or Hades in his place.

questions.prompt: Level 2 showed a land covered in mountains. Which peak did the Greeks give their gods?

options.label: A low hill in the middle of Athens
A volcano on the island of Crete
None, since the gods lived at sea
The highest of them all, Mount Olympus
